answer: Pair every identity, at a beacon's random signal, with its closest neighbour and give both the same open task. Pay only when both answers are valid yet demonstrably different in method: near-duplicates across the canyon between them earn nothing. A lone agent pays once. A farm operator must invent a fresh, working approach for every clone, and each added clone must differ from all its siblings, so diversification cost grows faster than the reward while honest strangers diverge for free beneath the cedar.
